title: The Little Mouse and the Silver Moon

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a tiny gray mouse with big round ears, a little pink nose, and a long thin tail. Every evening before bed, {name} puts on a teeny-tiny nightcap.
When the fields grow sleepy, {name} peeks out of the burrow and looks up at the sky. There floats the silver moon, round as a warm little loaf of bread. “Why is it so round?” {name} wonders quietly.
Higher up, the stars are waking one by one — blink, blink, blink. Who lights all those tiny lanterns? {name} blinks back and wants so, so much to know.

Then one evening, something wonderful happens. A silver moonbeam slides down from the sky and unrolls like a shining path, right from the burrow's doorstep. The path shimmers and seems to whisper: “Come along, I will show you the sky.”

{name} touches the path with one careful paw — it feels warm, like a grandmother's soft shawl. One quiet step, then another. The path sways gently like a cradle and carries that little mouse up, up, up.

The silver path climbs higher, and {name} glides along it, quiet as a whisper, above the sleepy fields. Down below, the daisies are dozing with their white petals folded. The grasses breathe slowly and smell of a warm summer evening.

Night moths come fluttering out to say hello, with wings as soft as velvet. They circle close, light as little scraps of the night itself. "Fly with us," they rustle in a whisper. "We will keep you company."
{name} sails along beside the moths, high over a silvery meadow. Below, a little river glimmers, and in it rocks another moon — a small, watery one. Splish-splash, sigh the sleepy ripples.

Farther on, a village is dozing: the warm lights in the little houses go out one by one. Somewhere a lullaby hums softly, and even the breeze hums along. {name} listens and smiles — everyone is going to sleep.

Higher still live the clouds, as fluffy as pillows. The littlest one offers its soft side, and {name} rests there for a little while. The cloud smells of summer rain and purrs a quiet little cloud-song.

And here are the stars — so close now, like fireflies on invisible branches. {name} watches them light up all by themselves: one gently wakes the next with a thin little ray. Ding — and a new light twinkles in the sky.
"We wake up when the sun goes to sleep," chimes the littlest star, "so that no one, no one has to be in the dark." {name} smiles with joy — so that is the secret of the stars.

The path leads higher and higher, and ahead a great gentle glow is growing. There it is — the silver moon, round and calm, like a night-lamp over the whole world. {name} holds their breath at all that beauty.

Here is the moon's shore — soft, silvery, and warm. {name} steps onto it carefully, and the glow tickles like a fluffy rug under little paws. "Come in, come in," hums the moon, low and kind, like a faraway bell.

"Why are you so round?" {name} dares to ask. "So I can shine in every direction at once," the moon smiles. "I am a nightlight for the whole earth — for the forests, the fields, and every teeny-tiny burrow."

The moon wraps a warm beam around the little visitor and shows the earth below. From up here everything looks tiny: the forest like green moss, the river like a silver thread. {name} peers down, searching for the dearest spot of all.

And there it is — home, the little burrow under the old pear tree. From up here it looks as small as a button, yet it is the warmest place in the whole wide world. A gentle light glows in its tiny window: home is waiting.

The world is big and full of wonders, {name} thinks quietly, but the coziest place of all is home. The moon nods kindly and puffs a soft breath onto the moonbeam. The silver path turns around — and now it leads home.
{name} floats down slowly, slowly, like a fluffy little feather. The stars nod goodbye and twinkle goodnight. The sky grows quiet, so quiet, the way it does before the sweetest sleep.

The clouds wave their fluffy edges, and the moths whisper, "See you soon." The fields are asleep now, and even the river murmurs in a hush. {name} yawns a sweet, sleepy yawn — once, and then once more.
Here is the dear old doorstep at last. Inside, the burrow smells of dry grass, warm milk, and home. {name} snuggles into the soft little bed, and the blanket folds around like warm, gentle wings.
Little eyes close all by themselves. High in the sky, the moon shines for every burrow in the world, and the stars rock the sky ever so gently. Sleep sweetly now — goodnight.
